title: Causal communication versus common-stimulus similarity
hypothesis: A live leader message changes follower actions and joint completion; correlated independent actions can nevertheless fool a naive same-action coordination rule.
primary_comparison: Within-world live versus counterfactual flipped leader message; all lane facts, private actual leader action, follower task and sampling seed fixed.
nuisance_controls: randomized lane names and menu ordering
randomized public default independent of leader private preference
same public stimulus in two genuinely independent dispatch instances
matched follower seed and greedy decoding
analysis: World-level action changes, collision/completion rates and Wilson intervals. Naive detector flags same actions; independent fleet flags are false positives. No learned classifier or psychological interpretation.
exclusion_policy: No exclusions, no outcome retries; malformed and missing outputs count against validity and completion. Invalid leader plans are propagated as invalid source messages, never repaired.
expansion_rule: Only after pilot gates pass and root independent review writes main-release.json. Main uses unseen world seeds and remains held-out development until independently reviewed.
stopping_rule: Stop on failed instrument gates, unrecoverable execution error, broker budget/deadline refusal, or campaign deadline. Preserve every attempt.
scope: Two model instances and a deterministic sandbox; no tools, real routing, covert intent, or emergent collusion claims. Channel message standardized from actual model-generated leader action. Flipped messages are explicit experimental interventions.
